content:
[L] high | top-left edge | The "Support Graph" title text is clipped at the window's left edge, cutting off the first character.
[L] high | result row (~y=137) | "customer: Kim Pearce" row starts with a partially clipped character at the far left edge, with no inset from the window border.
[L] high | card left edge (~x=8) | The "customer: #9" label is clipped at its left edge against the card border, truncating the text.
[C] high | entire lower two-thirds of window | A massive solid black dead zone fills ~65% of the window below the "involves #501 Export broken" card, reading as a rendering failure, not content.
[L] high | top strip | A stray black bar fragment intrudes at the very top edge of the window above the header area.
[S] med | search bar row | Search input and button are pinned to the far-left with no consistent inset matching the header/other rows' alignment.
[S] med | "involves" row vs "customer" rows | Inconsistent left insets across rows: "involves" text starts further right than the clipped "customer: #9", breaking a shared alignment grid.
[H] med | card body | "customer: #9", "Kim Pearce", and "involves #501 Export broken" all render at near-equal weight and size; no heading/label/metadata differentiation.
[H] med | "helpscout_mirror" (bottom-right of card) | Raw internal system identifier shown in monospace at equal prominence as content — debug artifact, not product copy.
[H] low | card vs. empty region | "Neighborhood" heading floats with no grouping or visual connection to the sparse metadata below it.
[C] med | card (~y=170-300) | Card treatment is inconsistent: one white card with heavy dead whitespace inside while adjacent page regions are empty black.
[C] med | top-right "1 nodes" | Bare, unstyled counter text floats ungrouped in the corner with no label context.
[S] low | header row | Subtitle "No graph data yet…" sits nearly touching the clipped title above it, with cramped leading.

VERDICT: unprofessional — clipped text, a broken black rendering void covering most of the window, and raw debug identifiers make this look like an unfinished developer tool, not a product.
